title: The Kingdom of Crooked Mirrors
author: Vitaly Gubarev
short_summary: A girl named Olya, who often makes excuses and avoids the truth, steps through a magic mirror into a strange kingdom where everything is reversed. There she meets her own mirror-twin, Yalo, and together they discover a kingdom ruled by a cruel boy-king, where flattery and lies are rewarded and honesty is dangerous.
extended_summary:
A girl named Olya, who often makes excuses and avoids the truth, steps through a magic mirror into a strange kingdom where everything is reversed. There she meets her own mirror-twin, Yalo, and together they discover a kingdom ruled by a cruel boy-king, where flattery and lies are rewarded and honesty is dangerous.

Olya and Yalo must work together — and tell the truth, even when it's frightening — to help a group of oppressed children and stand up to the unfair rules of the kingdom. By the end of their journey, Olya finally understands why honesty matters, even when a comfortable lie would be so much easier.

questions.prompt: How does Olya enter the kingdom of crooked mirrors?
questions.explanation: Olya steps through an old magic mirror, which is how she enters the reversed kingdom.

questions.prompt: Olya's mirror-twin in the kingdom is named ___.
questions.explanation: Yalo is Olya's own name spelled backward, and also her mirror-twin's name.

questions.prompt: Sort each behavior into the right group.

content.groupB: Punished or dangerous in the kingdom

questions.explanation: The kingdom's reversed rules mean flattery and lies are praised, while telling the truth is risky.

questions.prompt: Why do you think Olya needed to see her own flaws reflected in a mirror world to change?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — seeing a problem reflected back can make it easier to recognize in yourself.

questions.prompt: In the mirror kingdom, backward names are common. What does 'Yalo' spell if you reverse it?
questions.explanation: Yalo is simply Olya's name written backward — a small clue that hints at the kingdom's whole reversed logic before you even meet her.

questions.prompt: In this kingdom, telling the truth is dangerous, but telling a smooth ___ can win you favor at court.
questions.explanation: The kingdom rewards exactly the opposite of what Olya's own bad habits back home were built on — which is precisely the point.

questions.prompt: Put Olya's journey through the mirror kingdom in order.

items: Olya avoids telling the truth back in her own world
She steps through an old mirror into the reversed kingdom
She meets Yalo, her own mirror-twin, and sees the kingdom's unfair rules up close
Olya finally tells the truth, even though it's frightening, to help others

questions.explanation: Olya's journey mirrors her own growth — she starts by avoiding the truth and ends by choosing it, even when it's hard.

questions.prompt: Match each figure to their part in the mirror kingdom.

right: Arrives from the real world, used to dodging the truth
Olya's mirror-twin, born into this backward world
Rules by rewarding flattery and punishing honesty
Need Olya and Yalo's courage to be helped

questions.explanation: Olya and Yalo make an unlikely pair — one still learning the value of honesty, one who's lived her whole life without it being safe.

questions.prompt: In the real, non-mirror world, sort each behavior into the right group.

options.label: Telling the truth, even when it's uncomfortable
Making excuses to avoid getting in trouble
Flattering someone just to win their favor
Standing up for someone being treated unfairly

questions.explanation: Notice that the mirror kingdom rewards exactly the habits from Group B and punishes the ones from Group A — that's the whole joke of a 'crooked' kingdom.

questions.prompt: If YOU stepped through a mirror into a kingdom where lying was rewarded and honesty was risky, do you think you'd act like Olya at the start of the story, or like Olya at the end? Why?
questions.explanation: There's no single right answer — the story is really asking whether courage to be honest is something you already have, or something you grow into.
